page.description: XCP-ng editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A free, open-source fork of XenServer: a bare-metal hypervisor with pools, live migration and shared storage, administered from Xen Orchestra or the command line.
pros: Free hypervisor with the enterprise features of its upstream (pools, live migration, snapshots).
Managed from Xen Orchestra, including a web UI.
Compatible with the XenAPI tooling built for XenServer.
cons: The public mirror publishes only upgrade-only ISOs; the fresh-install ISO is not offered there, so no image can be pinned.
Management normally means running Xen Orchestra as a separate appliance.
Hardware compatibility is narrower than on a general-purpose Linux.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for XCP-ng; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Install from the ISO that XCP-ng publishes for the release, then manage the host from Xen Orchestra. Installing erases the target disk.
